hints: Look at Faye's statement. With only three suspects, what does "either Nico or I" tell you about Linus?
Faye's statement means Linus didn't do it, which is just what Nico says. So those two statements are true together or false together.
Only one statement is false, and it can't come from that pair. So Linus's is false, and Nico left the pen open.

solution.key_idea: Faye's statement says the same as Nico's, that Linus didn't do it, so the one false statement must be Linus's.
steps: Exactly two of the three statements are true, so exactly one is false.
Faye says Nico or Faye did it. With only three suspects, that means Linus didn't, which is exactly what Nico says.
So Nico's and Faye's statements are true together or false together. Both false would make two false statements, so both are true.
That leaves Linus's statement as the false one. Linus says Nico didn't leave the pen open, so Nico did.
Check Nico: two true statements and one false, as the rule says. Testing Faye gives three true, and testing Linus only one.
solution.epilogue: Nico, in the middle of a long story, had let himself into the pen to scratch Clementine's ears and left the latch undone. He paid for both pies, though he still swore it was twelve.

answer_line: Nico left the goat pen open.
